title: Universal colimits and cartesian pushout gluing in spaces
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use spaces and coherent diagrams of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. The infinity category $\mathcal S$ is presentable and has finite limits. All pullbacks and colimits below are infinity-categorical. Colimits in $\mathcal S$ are universal in the following explicit sense: for a small simplicial set $K$, a coherent diagram $D:K\to\mathcal S$ with colimit cocone $D\to L$, and maps $L\to B\leftarrow C$ of small spaces, the induced cocone $D(k)\times_B C\to L\times_B C$ is colimiting.

Put $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal S)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal S)$. A morphism of arrows is called cartesian when its naturality square in $\mathcal S$ is a pullback. In every pushout square of arrows with vertices $a,b,c,d$ and arrows $a\to b$, $a\to c$, $b\to d$, $c\to d$, if $a\to b$ and $a\to c$ are cartesian, then $b\to d$ and $c\to d$ are cartesian.
